title: 蚂蚁百灵发布 Ling-3.2-flash：原生多模态，560B 总参数单步激活 25B
content:
公众号：蚂蚁百灵· 百灵大模型·· 5 小时前精选AI 评分66
蚂蚁百灵发布 Ling-3.2-flash：原生多模态，560B 总参数单步激活 25B
Ling-3.2-flash 正式上线：原生多模态，视觉反馈支撑更可靠的执行与交付
AI 导读
蚂蚁百灵发布原生多模态模型 Ling-3.2-flash，总参数 560B、单步激活 25B，支持 1M 原生长上下文，重点强化视觉反馈自检与异常自适应恢复能力。
推荐理由
原文给出 Ling-3.2-flash 的参数规模、视觉自检与异常恢复机制和推理加速数据，可据此判断其在长程任务中的可用性。
来源：公众号：蚂蚁百灵 · mp.weixin.qq.com

report.summary: Ant Group's BaiLing team released Ling-3.2-flash, a natively multimodal sparse MoE model with 560B total and 25B active parameters, 1M context, and visual self-checking for long-horizon agent tasks.
report.background: Chinese labs have spent the past year converging on sparse Mixture-of-Experts designs, which raise total capacity while keeping per-token compute low — the same trade-off DeepSeek, Qwen and Kimi have pursued. A second front is multimodality: most models bolt a vision encoder onto a text backbone, which limits cross-modal reasoning. "Native" multimodal training fuses modalities from the start. A third front is reliability. As models are deployed as agents that run dozens of steps, errors compound; letting a model look at screenshots or rendered output of its own work and correct itself has become a practical fix. Ant Group's BaiLing (Ling) line has released open-weight models including Ling and the Ring reasoning series, positioning itself in both the open-source and enterprise API markets. Ling-3.2-flash lands in that context: bigger total capacity, smaller activation, longer context, and an explicit bet that visual feedback loops matter more than raw benchmark gains for real task completion.
key_points: Sparse MoE at 560B total / 25B active: the model holds far more parameters than it computes per token, so serving cost tracks the 25B active slice rather than the full 560B. That is the standard recipe for getting large-model quality at mid-size inference bills — attractive for high-volume API traffic.

Native multimodality: vision and language are trained together rather than stitched afterwards. In practice this should help on tasks where the model must read charts, screenshots or UI layouts, and reduces the awkward handoff that plagues adapter-based multimodal models.

1M native long context: the window is trained in, not extended by post-hoc tricks, which matters for repository-scale code, long documents and multi-hour agent sessions where earlier context must stay usable.

Visual feedback self-checking: the model can inspect rendered output or screenshots of its own actions and correct course. Paired with anomaly-adaptive recovery — detecting when a step failed and retrying differently — this targets the compounding-error problem in long agent runs.

Reported inference acceleration data: the release includes speedup figures alongside the architecture claims, the practical signal for teams deciding whether it is servable at acceptable latency and cost.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Ling-3.2-flash reinforces two trends: sparse MoE as the default architecture for frontier-scale models, and self-verification via visual feedback as the next frontier for agents rather than raw benchmark scores. It also adds another credible Chinese open-weight option, intensifying price pressure on API providers. For developers, a 25B-active model with 1M context and native vision is a plausible fit for coding agents, browser automation and document pipelines — but the real test is whether the self-check loop measurably cuts failed task runs, and whether serving a 560B MoE is feasible outside well-provisioned clusters. For regular users, the near-term effect is more reliable multi-step assistants that catch their own mistakes, plus cheaper multimodal features as competition compresses prices.
report.tools: Watch the BaiLing / inclusionAI releases on Hugging Face and ModelScope, where Ant has published open weights for the Ling and Ring series; check whether Ling-3.2-flash weights follow. For serving, vLLM and SGLang both handle MoE models with expert parallelism and are the usual first stop. For agent loops that exploit visual self-checking, pair the model with browser or GUI automation harnesses such as Playwright or OS-level sandbox environments. If you only need the API, benchmark it against your own long-horizon tasks before migrating.
